## `delivery.mjs` in use

Every caller is a worker of a task declared in another pack. Three real shapes:

**Land a regenerated file on the executor's target PR** (canon-curation's pack-version-history worker):

```js
import { deliverGenerated } from '../../../claudinite-tasks/public/delivery.mjs';

const pr = await deliverGenerated({
  root, repo, base, token, stamp: today, branchPrefix: PR_BRANCH_PREFIX, log,
  branch: process.env.CLAUDINITE_TARGET_BRANCH || null,
  pr: process.env.CLAUDINITE_TARGET_PR ? Number(process.env.CLAUDINITE_TARGET_PR) : null,
  task: TASK_ID,
  files,
  message: `Claudinite: pack version history\n\n${AUTOMERGE_TRAILER}: ${policyExpression(task.automerge)}`,
  title: 'Claudinite: pack version history',
  body: [...],
});
```

That one call is what the local rule "land a regenerated file through deliver-generated, reading prior state from the fetched base" refers to. It fetches the base, compares trees, pushes only on a difference, and opens or amends the PR the executor handed in.

**Push a commit onto the base branch with the task trailer** (pack-version-bump, cloudflare site-release):

```js
import { baseTip, readAt, remoteUrl, withTaskTrailer } from '../../../claudinite-tasks/public/delivery.mjs';

const parent  = baseTip(root, remote, base);
const pkgText = readAt(root, parent, 'package.json');
pushOnto(git, { remote, baseSha: tip, branch: base, files,
  message: withTaskTrailer(`Release site version ${version}`, taskId) });
```

The trailer is how the queue later attributes the commit to the task that made it. A worker that forgot it would produce commits the mechanism cannot account for.

**Deliver a PR and merge or park it by the executor's verdict** (lifecycle's update worker):

```js
import { deliveryFor, openDeliveredPull, disposeOpenPull, pullCreateError, landDelivery, withTaskTrailer }
  from '../../../claudinite-tasks/public/delivery.mjs';

const delivery  = deliveryFor(declaration);                 // member asked for review, or land
const incumbent = openDeliveredPull(open.json, UPDATE_PREFIX);
if (incumbent) await disposeOpenPull({ ... });              // close last cycle's PR
...
const failure = pullCreateError(created.status, created.json);
if (failure) throw new Error(`could not open the update PR: ${failure}`);
if (terminal.action === 'merge') await landDelivery({ token, repo, base, pr, delivery, task: UPDATE_TASK_ID });
```

## `github.mjs` in use

```js
import { makeGh, findOrCreateTracker, writeTracker } from '../../../claudinite-tasks/public/github.mjs';
const gh = makeGh();                                              // token + retry + status-aware fetch
const { number: tracker } = await findOrCreateTracker(gh, repo, TRACKER_TITLE);
await writeTracker(gh, repo, tracker, { body, comment });         // basics' ci-performance
```

```js
import { makeGh, dispatchWorkflow } from '../../../claudinite-tasks/public/github.mjs';
const sent = await dispatchWorkflow(gh, repo, WORKFLOW_FILE, ref); // dashboard's publish-pages
if (!sent.ok && sent.status === 404) throw new NeedsHuman('action', `${WORKFLOW_FILE} is not on ${ref}`);
```

Growth-dedup takes only `makeGh`. The two workflow file-name constants are exported but nothing outside takes them.

Grouped as I would write the file. Right column is the value on `main` today.

| File | What it imports | Free of `src/`? |

| `work-item-grammar.mjs` | the constants only | yes, same move: the 20 parsers become the implementation, `src/items/work-item.mjs` imports them |
| `task-declaration.mjs` | `src/contract/` (task-contract, precondition, task-terms, merge-policy), which reaches the engine's check helpers and pack registry | no |
| `delivery.mjs` | `src/deliver/` and `src/world/` (github, clock, processes, actions), the engine's settings reader | no |
| `github.mjs` | `src/world/github.mjs`, `src/world/actions.mjs`, `src/items/tracker.mjs` | no |

The distinction is what each file promises. The first two are the wire vocabulary, and the right shape is for them to *be* the definition, with the scheduler importing from `public/` rather than `public/` re-exporting from `src/`. That inverts today's direction for those two files, and it is the change that makes "no dependency on src" true and testable.

The other three are the machinery's own operations offered under a stable name. `landDelivery` cannot be written without the GitHub client, the clock and the trailer logic, and `normalizeTaskDeclaration` is the loader. Moving their bodies into `public/` would put half of `src/` there. What they promise is that the name and signature hold, not that the implementation is self-contained.

Yes for `github.mjs`, and the tree supports it better than I expected. What the three backing modules actually hold:

| Backing module | Size | Public names | Internal importers | Inversion |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `src/world/github.mjs` | 301 lines, 35 exports | `makeGh`, `dispatchWorkflow` | 17 modules | the two public names are self-contained: `makeGh` is 25 lines over `fetch` with no imports, `dispatchWorkflow` is 6 lines over `gh`. Move them into `public/github.mjs`; `src/world/github.mjs` imports `makeGh` from there and keeps its 33 one-line REST helpers, which nothing outside takes. |
| `src/world/actions.mjs` | 71 lines | the two workflow file names | many | nothing outside takes those two constants, so they leave `public/` and `actions.mjs` is untouched. |
| `src/items/tracker.mjs` | 124 lines, 6 exports | `findOrCreateTracker`, `writeTracker` | **none** | its only importer in the whole pack is `public/github.mjs`. The scheduler never writes a tracker issue; it is purely a tool for workers. The whole file moves into `public/`. |

One wrinkle: the tracker calls five one-liners from `src/world/github.mjs` (`searchIssues`, `patchIssue`, `postIssue`, `setIssueBody`, `comment`). If `src/world/github.mjs` imports `makeGh` from `public/github.mjs` and `public/github.mjs` imports those five back, that is a cycle. The clean form spells those five REST calls directly against `gh` inside the tracker code, since each is one line. Then `public/github.mjs` imports nothing at all, and it is the implementation that `src/` builds on.

**The same question for `delivery.mjs`** splits three ways:

- `deliverGenerated` and its helpers (`baseTip`, `readAt`, `remoteUrl`), 161 lines: the only internal importers are two of this pack's own task workers, which are the same audience as any other pack's workers. The file moves into `public/` whole. It still imports the landing and world layers underneath, so it is a public tool built on `src/`, not free of it.
- `withTaskTrailer`, a 43-line format module with 5 internal importers: pure, so the trailer name goes into the constants file and the function into the grammar file, and `src/` imports it from there.
- `deliveryFor`, `landDelivery`, `openDeliveredPull`, `disposeOpenPull`, `pullCreateError`: five names out of the 633-line, 30-export landing module the executor itself runs on. Their only outside consumer is lifecycle's update worker, which lands its own PR the way the executor would. Not invertible; this stays a facade over `src/deliver/land-pr.mjs`.

**Resulting shape**

| File | Holds | Depends on `src/` |

- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.

- committing: How a commit is cut — one concern per commit, the issue it references, a landed commit revised only by a new one, files staged by name. Use before any git commit.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- fetching-from-the-web: Reading a page or a file from the web in a session — exact bytes over a summarizing fetch, and what a 403 or an egress block means. Use before any WebFetch or curl, and when a fetch is denied.

Use from a canon when a project's evidence shows a facet its shelf does not yet home — the curation stages' pack-writing method, and an owner's when asking what a project has taught the shelf.

                            (parseWorkItemTitle, parseWorkItemBody, parseRequestFields, statusOf,
                            outcomeOf, isQueueItem, isParked, parkKindOf, withMachineBlock,
                            taskIdFromPath, pickOrder, …) plus withTaskTrailer.

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.
